pairs_touching.notes_for_p3b: High row overlap (shared S0070-S0080, S0206 source ids) confirms this is not coincidental co-occurrence but a genuine general-model/specific-aggregate containment.
pairs_touching.what_says_this: Rows are near-identical/overlapping across both labels (e.g. S0071 'WorkItem is tested and confirmed as the aggregate root...' appears verbatim in both samples). The BC-7 tactical domain-model discovery (KOS-ARCH-BASELINE-003, S0070) explicitly concludes WorkItem as its aggregate root after rejecting Assignment/Workflow/Human Act as candidates (S0071), i.e. workitem-aggregate is the specific accepted realization/component that IS the bc7-domain-model's central deliverable, with bc7-domain-model additionally covering broader governance (open questions OQ-1..OQ-11, verification passes S0072-S0080) not part of the aggregate design itself.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: If bc7-domain-model turns out to also seriously model a second, co-equal aggregate root (not just WorkItem) that carries independent weight, the whole/part SPECIALIZATION framing would be wrong and this would be closer to co-occurrence-only UNWITNESSED.

pairs_touching.notes_for_p3b: Structurally similar to a schema/instance or constraint-set/entity pairing rather than any of the 11 enumerated relationship types; recommend P3b consider whether these should be modeled as one combined family (WorkItem aggregate + its invariant catalog) rather than two separate reconciliation objects.
pairs_touching.what_says_this: a and b are extracted from the same continuous body of evidence (S0071-S0078, S0206, S0234) documenting the AIP/BC-7 WorkItem tactical-model review: a catalogs the specific invariants (I-1..I-10, G-1/G-2, R-34, INV-ATTR-2, AIP-11, AIP-14) while b is the aggregate root (WorkItem) that those very invariants are internal to -- e.g. b's S0071 row states 'WorkItem is tested and confirmed as the aggregate root: its identity, lifecycle, four invariants (I-1..I-4)... are all internal to it,' and a's S0071 row analyzes 'I-4 is itself a spanning invariant' for the same aggregate. This is a constraint-list-to-entity relationship (the invariant catalog describes what the workitem aggregate must satisfy), not a continuity/derivation relationship between two distinct concepts.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: If the invariant catalog were shown to span multiple aggregates beyond WorkItem (making it a genuinely independent cross-cutting registry rather than this aggregate's own constraint set), a different characterization (e.g. INDEPENDENT or a broader registry relationship) might be warranted -- but the sampled evidence shows near-total overlap specific to WorkItem's own invariants.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Candidate A — Work Item Aggregate ... Result: passes every test. Critically, all four invariants are internal to it
rationale_evidence.statement: WorkItem is tested and confirmed as the aggregate root: its identity, lifecycle, four invariants (I-1..I-4), and consistency boundary are all internal to a single JSON record, needing no cross-record data to enforce.

rationale_evidence.anchor: one aggregate with two parts, or two aggregates sharing an identity? ... I-4 is itself a spanning invariant — a negative one.
rationale_evidence.statement: Facing evidence that no positive invariant spans the lifecycle and authority parts of the record (an honest finding that argues for splitting), the proposal nonetheless keeps one root because I-4 (they must never merge) is a negative spanning invariant needing a single holder that can see both parts, and the write boundary is one file.

rationale_evidence.anchor: (D) invariant violation — NO ... (D), and the defect is in the proposal's I-5 row, not in the invariant, the mechanism, or the model.
rationale_evidence.statement: C-3's classification is independently derived (before reading the refinement's own reasoning) as (D): the observed non-Governance recorder on a HANDOFF transition is not an invariant violation, missing enforcement, or a missing conceptual distinction, but simply a table cell in the proposal that measured I-5 (an authority-part invariant) against a lifecycle-part transition, which I-4 itself forbids conflating.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Verdict: (D) — a mis-scoped invariant statement. ... D.1 — The observation and the invariant live in different parts of the aggregate.
rationale_evidence.statement: Independent classification (derived from evidence E-1..E-8 before considering any candidate) concludes (D): the observed `architecture`-recorded HANDOFF is not a violation, missing enforcement, or missing distinction, but a case of measuring an authority-part invariant (I-5) against a lifecycle-part transition, which I-4 itself forbids; both instances were also the mechanism's required actor (DP-3), and a HANDOFF confers no ownership regardless.

rationale_evidence.anchor: The clearest consistency boundary in EKS, and it is IMPLICIT. ... Verdict: CONSISTENCY BOUNDARY — YES (class B). AGGREGATE — NOT ESTABLISHED.
rationale_evidence.statement: The work-item record is found to be the clearest consistency boundary in EKS (one file per item, atomic tmp+rename write, every precondition evaluated only against that record's own fold, R7 contract test pinning cross-item isolation) yet is IMPLICIT -- no WorkItem type, identity object, encapsulation, or invariant owner exists (invariants live in a free function, assertTransitionAllowed, outside the thing they protect), and the record holds two independent internal records (transitions, grants) with different writers/lifecycles, unusual for a single aggregate. Verdict: CONSISTENCY BOUNDARY = YES (class B); AGGREGATE = NOT ESTABLISHED.

## Rationale

WorkItem is tested and confirmed as the aggregate root: its identity, lifecycle, four invariants (I-1..I-4), and consistency boundary are all internal to a single JSON record, needing no cross-record data to enforce [S0071]. Additionally, Facing evidence that no positive invariant spans the lifecycle and authority parts of the record (an honest finding that argues for splitting), the proposal nonetheless keeps one root because I-4 (they must never merge) is a negative spanning invariant needing a single holder that can see both parts, and the write boundary is one file [S0071]. Further, C-3's classification is independently derived (before reading the refinement's own reasoning) as (D): the observed non-Governance recorder on a HANDOFF transition is not an invariant violation, missing enforcement, or a missing conceptual distinction, but simply a table cell in the proposal that measured I-5 (an authority-part invariant) against a lifecycle-part transition, which I-4 itself forbids conflating [S0073]. Relatedly, Independent classification (derived from evidence E-1..E-8 before considering any candidate) concludes (D): the observed `architecture`-recorded HANDOFF is not a violation, missing enforcement, or missing distinction, but a case of measuring an authority-part invariant (I-5) against a lifecycle-part transition, which I-4 itself forbids; both instances were also the mechanism's required actor (DP-3), and a HANDOFF confers no ownership regardless [S0078]. In the same vein, The work-item record is found to be the clearest consistency boundary in EKS (one file per item, atomic tmp+rename write, every precondition evaluated only against that record's own fold, R7 contract test pinning cross-item isolation) yet is IMPLICIT -- no WorkItem type, identity object, encapsulation, or invariant owner exists (invariants live in a free function, assertTransitionAllowed, outside the thing they protect), and the record holds two independent internal records (transitions, grants) with different writers/lifecycles, unusual for a single aggregate. Verdict: CONSISTENCY BOUNDARY = YES (class B); AGGREGATE = NOT ESTABLISHED [S0206].
